headline: Chips Crack, Gulf Tensions Simmer as Markets Eye Monday
body_html:
Friday's session, November 13, ended in a near stalemate beneath the surface: 335 of the 666 stocks we track rose and 324 fell. The pain was concentrated in one corner. Semiconductors dropped 3.6% as a group, and AMD slid 8.75%, with Alpha and Omega Semiconductor and PDF Solutions also sharply lower.

Financials gave up 1.35% and materials lost 0.79%. Consumer shares gained 0.96% and energy rose 0.89%, while homebuilders added 0.47% and industrials 0.37%. Healthcare and software finished roughly flat. Single-stock swings were large: Modine surged 27.86%, Stantec rose 14.06%, and Heartflow plunged 19.13%.

Looking to Monday, November 16, the docket is dominated by geopolitics. Reports of tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz and missile interceptions across the Gulf sit against word that the White House may hold off on Iran strikes absent fresh provocations. Traders will watch whether energy's firmness holds, and whether Friday's chip selling spreads or stabilizes.

briefs.headline: Hormuz mine reports put shipping on alert
briefs.body: Iran's navy said three tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Any confirmation of lasting disruption to the waterway would matter for energy shippers and for the sector that finished Friday up 0.89%. Monday's trading will test how seriously markets take the reports.

briefs.headline: Gulf air defenses busy across the region
briefs.body: Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, while Tehran claimed it struck a US base. Separately, a Saudi-led coalition reported shooting down missiles headed for Riyadh and drones over the Eastern Province. The exchanges raise the risk premium traders attach to the region.

briefs.headline: Washington signals restraint on Iran, for now
briefs.body: Sources say the president told advisers he may hold off on attacks against Iran if there are no new provocations. That conditional pause offers some relief, but it leaves markets exposed to any incident that changes the calculation as the week opens.

briefs.headline: Houthis gain ground near a key chokepoint
briefs.body: Yemeni government forces pulled back from an area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving Houthi fighters in control. The narrow passage is a major shipping lane, so the shift adds a second maritime pressure point alongside Hormuz for investors to follow.

briefs.headline: Starship catch marks a spaceflight first
briefs.body: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket, a first for the program. The feat points toward reusable orbital vehicles and should keep attention on space-related stocks, though Friday's market was driven far more by the chip selloff and Gulf headlines.

briefs.headline: Storage lots draw institutional money
briefs.body: Rising rents are pulling Wall Street capital into industrial outdoor storage, where investors buy lots used to park trucks, trailers and equipment. The trend shows institutions hunting for yield in niche property types, even as homebuilders rose 0.47% Friday.
